# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 38 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_038_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 8 — Abstain from Evil; Practice Good

**1** I said to him, "Sir, I ask you now to show me the powers of the evil spirits, so that by recognizing their deeds I may keep away from them." **2** He replied, "Listen to the deeds from which you must abstain. Abstain from evil-speaking, from adultery, from drunkenness, from wicked pleasure, from unlawful eating, from pride and boasting, from lying and theft, and from all such things. **3** Do you think these are small evils for a servant of God? They are not — adultery is a great evil, and drunkenness is a great evil, and pride and boasting are great evils. These great evils are what servants of God must abstain from." **4** "Hear now also the works you must practice: help the widow; visit the orphan and the poor; redeem the servants of God from their tribulation; be hospitable to strangers; resist no one; be humble and more submissive than all men; honor the elderly; practice righteousness; watch over brotherly love; endure injury with patience; bear no grudge; encourage those who are sick in soul; do not cast away those who have stumbled in faith but restore and encourage them; rebuke sinners; do not oppress debtors and the poor — and all similar things." **5** "Do you think these are small goods for those who practice them?" "Not at all," he said. "They are very great." **6** I said, "Sir, I would like to know which of these evils I am caught in, so that I may turn from them." "Listen," he replied, "and I will tell you. Your business dealings and the many transactions you have undertaken — do not let these consume you; leave business aside and cling to righteousness. **7** For if you do not disentangle yourself from your many business dealings, you will not be able to keep the Lord's commandments. And if you do not keep the Lord's commandments, you will not be saved."

---

### Council Notes

Mandate 8 is the Shepherd's comprehensive ethical catalog — the most complete list of dos and don'ts in the twelve mandates.

**The abstention list (v. 2-3):** evil-speaking, adultery, drunkenness, wicked pleasure, unlawful eating, pride, boasting, lying, theft. These represent the classic "works of the flesh" tradition (cf. Gal 5:19-21).

**The practice list (v. 4):** The list of positive works is remarkable for its social orientation — it is organized around care for the vulnerable:
- Widows, orphans, the poor (the traditional OT triad of the helpless)
- Strangers (hospitality to outsiders)
- Those in distress
- The spiritually sick
- Those who have stumbled in faith

The list bridges the Old Testament prophetic tradition (Isaiah 1:17: "seek justice, rebuke the oppressor, defend the orphan, plead for the widow") with New Testament community ethics (James 1:27; Matthew 25:35-40).

The personal application to Hermas (v. 6-7) — his business dealings as a specific spiritual obstacle — connects the mandate back to the recurring Hermaic concern: wealth and commercial entanglement as the primary distraction from righteous living.
